headline: Basecamp values simplicity, craft, and calm work—rejecting hype while emphasizing long-term stability and asynchronous communication.
identity: Basecamp has consistently valued craft, altruism (treating people right), and a calm, sustainable approach to work across its 24-year history. The company's language around craft peaked in 2021 (zscore 1.30) but has declined notably since, dropping to -0.78 by 2025—a shift away from emphasizing meticulous product design toward operational and policy documentation. Altruism language strengthened from 2014 onward (zscore 0.15 to 0.99 by 2021), then stabilized around 0.57–0.67, showing sustained commitment to treating people well. Wellbeing language surged dramatically from 2019 onward, peaking in 2022 (zscore 1.25), reflecting a deliberate pivot toward asynchronous work, remote flexibility, and protection of focus—a core identity shift that has persisted.
fit: You might be a good fit if you are self-directed, value deep work over constant communication, and believe that sustainable pace and clarity matter more than hustle. Basecamp explicitly seeks 'managers of one' who thrive with autonomy, can work asynchronously across time zones, and embrace a 'calm company' ethos. You should also be comfortable with their apolitical stance on internal discourse (introduced 2022) and their rejection of 'peak performance' culture.

sections.heading: The Craft-to-Operations Pivot (2009–2025)
sections.body: From 2009 to 2021, Basecamp's careers copy leaned heavily on craft—quality, attention to detail, and building 'the best product in the business.' The craft zscore peaked at 1.30 in 2021 with language like 'Full attention is required to do great work' and emphasis on rigorous care for products. However, by 2023–2025, craft language collapsed to -0.58 to -0.78, a dramatic reversal. The shift reflects a move away from selling the company as a design/product powerhouse toward positioning it as a well-run operational entity. Quotes shifted from 'Quality, clarity, attention to detail' (2009–2021) to procedural guidance: 'Below you'll find a collection of general principles we try to keep in mind at 37signals when making decisions' (2025). This is not a loss of values but a reframing—the company still cares about craft, but no longer leads with it in recruitment messaging.

sections.heading: The Wellbeing & Async Revolution (2019–2022)
sections.body: Wellbeing language was nearly absent before 2019 (zscore -0.88 to -1.02), but surged starting in 2019 (zscore 1.57) and peaked in 2022 (zscore 1.25). This coincides with the publication of their internal handbook and explicit anti-chat messaging. Key phrases emerged: 'Give people long uninterrupted stretches to get work done' (2021), 'Then others can read it on their schedule, when the natural lulls of the day allow it, rather than being interrupted right in their peak flow time' (2022). By 2020, the company was explicitly rejecting 'CRUSHING IT' and 'PEAK PERFORMANCE' culture. This wasn't a gradual evolution—it was a deliberate repositioning of the company as a refuge from interrupt-driven work, a stance that has remained consistent through 2026.

sections.heading: Altruism & Inclusion: Steady but Cautious (2014–2026)
sections.body: Altruism language rose from -0.49 (2010) to 0.15 (2014) and climbed to 0.99 by 2021, driven by language about 'giving back,' 'treating people right,' and 'positive impact on the world.' However, inclusion language (DEI) remained modest and cautious. The term 'diversity' appeared only in 2017 with a high score (0.55), but explicit demographic or structural inclusion language never dominated. By 2022, the company introduced an explicitly apolitical stance: 'We respect everyone's right to participate in political expression and activism, but we avoid having political debates on our internal co[mmunications].' This signals a deliberate choice to frame inclusion as belonging and respect rather than as demographic representation or systemic change—a positioning that has held steady through 2026.
